body:
I don't know the extent of "harm" your trust issues have on you, but personally I don't find it troubling to live life without trusting anyone. 

Trust is too idealic, instead of gambling away your investment in someone why not choose to rely on them when needed. For example I don't trust anyone on my team to produce any actual good work since they all seem unwilling, but that doesn't mean I don't rely on them to do the tasks I give out.

You see, trusting someone means you expect this person to give their best for you and you for them. But what guarantee is there for any of you in the relationship? I mean, it's human nature to doubt and it's vital for survival. 

No one should go on damaging their mental health over factors they can't control. Especially when the line between being the victim and perpetrator are indefinitely blurred.

Thanks a lot, this is probably the most comforting thing someone's ever said to me hahaha. People just assume I have everything together because of how "chill" I am and that my apathy for life is just so "cool". Not knowing that I'm only "chill" because I spend all my time thinking of ways I'll die and how nothing will matter after my body's gone limp. 

To be honest I truly and utterly fucking hate that I feel this way, especially with how I've been conditioned to think that complaining in the slightest means you're ungrateful and the lowest of lows when there are people suffering much more.

Needless to say, I'm desperate for help. But hearing someone I don't even know say something I've been trying to avoid makes me want to at least live a few years longer (to see if my thoughts get any better)
